land.text: the interior of Oman, 'north to Ibri and south to the Alsharqiyah region and the Sharqiya Sands', between the Hajar Mountains and the Rub' al Khali, which seceded from the Sultan at Muscat in 1913

predecessors.note: The sultanate-of-oman dossier (written for the merged Sultanate of Oman and Sultanate of Muscat and Oman rows) records the same loss in 1913.

land.text: the interior, taken over in January 1959: 'With the defeat of the Imam, the Treaty of Seeb was terminated and the autonomous Imamate of Oman was abolished'

successors.note: Handed over in January 1959 (Jebel Akhdar War page: the Imamate 'was defeated in January 1959'; the SAS occupied Saiq and Shuraijah on 30 January 1959). The region's year 1919 is the year of Cliopatria's last Imamate shape, not the date of the handover. The sultanate-of-oman dossier draws the interior as the Sultan's vassal from 25 September 1920 to 1954, contests it 1954-1959 and gains it in 1959.

capitals.name: Nizwa
capitals.note: Treaty of Seeb page: the capital was established at Nizwa; the Imamate page: the capital 'alternated historically between Rustaq and Nizwa'. Jebel Akhdar War page: the Sultanate captured Nizwa on 15 December 1955 (the Treaty of Seeb page: 'In 1955 Sultan Said bin Taimour occupied the capital, Nizwa'), the Imamate 'continued for a short time to lead a temporary government-in-exile from Dammam, Saudi Arabia' (undated), and its forces freed Nizwa in the 1957 uprising; the dot stays at Nizwa.

rulers.name: Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi
rulers.title: Imam
rulers.note: Treaty of Seeb page: 'Imam Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi was murdered in July 1924'; the Imamate page: he 'instigated an anti-Muscat rebellion' in 1913. No page read gives his election date, so 1913 is the year of the rebellion. The Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi article named by the reviewer returned url_not_found.

rulers.name: Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Khalili
rulers.title: Imam
rulers.note: Treaty of Seeb page: elected as the new Imam after Salim's murder in July 1924 (the page gives no year for the election, so 1924 is the year of the murder); his death is undated on both pages and preceded Ghalib's election on 3 May 1954 (Jebel Akhdar War page), so the last year is given as 1954 and overlaps Ghalib's first.

rulers.name: Ghalib al-Hinai
rulers.title: Imam
rulers.note: Jebel Akhdar War page: elected on 3 May 1954 after Imam Alkhalili died (Treaty of Seeb page: 'elected in 1954'); after the defeat of January 1959 he went into exile in Saudi Arabia.

keyframe_review.note: 103.9 k km2 (453 cells) for 1913-1918: Ad Dakhiliyah (115 of 146 cells), Ad Dhahirah (120 of 131), Ash Sharqiyah (147 of 151) and parts of Al Batinah and Al Buraymi, with Nizwa, Ibri, Rustaq, Bahla, Izki and Ibra inside; the page: the Imamate 'extended north to Ibri and south to the Alsharqiyah region and the Sharqiya Sands', bounded by the Hajar Mountains and the Rub' al Khali, so the shape fits. It also takes the coastal cell at Sur, which the page does not give it. The Imamate page has no infobox area ('Area: Not stated'), so no ratio could be taken.

correction.text: the interior shape unchanged, for 1919 only; the next keyframe carries the same polygon for 1920-1959

keyframe_review.note: Same polygon as 1913 for 1919 (103.9 k km2). The rebellion 'lasted until 1920' and the Treaty of Seeb was signed on 25 September 1920 (11 Muharram 1339); Cliopatria's row ends in 1919, so the years from 1920 are in the next keyframe. The Imamate page has no infobox area ('Area: Not stated'), so no ratio could be taken.

correction.text: the interior shape unchanged, with the years extended from 1920 to January 1959: autonomous under the Sultan's sovereignty to October 1954, contested with him in the Jebel Akhdar War to January 1959

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Imamate row ends in 1919, but the Imamate page's infobox reads 'End of the Jebel Akhdar War: 1959', the page says the Sultanate 'was able to defeat the Imamate in Jebel Akhdar War that lasted until 1959', and the Treaty of Seeb page says the treaty 'granted autonomy to the imamate in the interior of Oman but recognized the sovereignty of the' Sultanate of Muscat. No page gives a change of frontier for 1920-1954, so the 1919 polygon (103.9 k km2) is kept. From 25 October 1954 the whole interior is a contested zone (ledger and war), drawn as a blend, so the shape is not cut when the Sultanate took Nizwa on 15 December 1955 (Jebel Akhdar War page; the Treaty of Seeb page also has 1955) and the Imamate's forces freed Nizwa, Firq, Izki, Tanuf, Bahla and the Jebel Akhdar in the 1957 uprising; the pages do not say what the Imamate held in 1956 ('the red flag of the Sultanate flew over the interior for the first time in half a century') or when the Muscat Regiment suppressed the rising at Nizwa, and Ibri stayed occupied. Same Cliopatria polygon includes a coastal cell at Sur that the Imamate page does not support. No infobox area on either page.

region.text: Nizwa, the capital of the revived Imamate

ledger.note: 1913: Imam Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi revives the Imamate of Oman at Nizwa and rebels against Muscat. 'In 1913, Imam Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi instigated an anti-Muscat rebellion that lasted until 1920.' The Treaty of Seeb page: he revived the Imamate and the capital was established at Nizwa. The pages give neither a month nor an election date.

region.text: the interior of Oman between Ibri and the Sharqiyah, separated from Muscat by the Hajar Mountains

ledger.note: 1913: the interior passes from Muscat to the Imamate. The Imamate's territory 'extended north to Ibri and south to the Alsharqiyah region and the Sharqiya Sands', bounded by the Hajar Mountains and the Rub' al Khali; the page gives no town-by-town conquest.

region.text: the interior held by the Imamate against the Sultan at Muscat

ledger.note: 1913: the rebellion against the Sultan begins and runs to 1920. The page gives the span, not a first campaign.

1920: the Treaty of Seeb ends the rebellion. Signed on 25 September 1920, mediated by Ronald Wingate, the British political agent at Muscat; the Imamate page: 'The treaty resulted in a de facto split between Oman and Muscat'.

region.text: the interior, autonomous under the Sultan's sovereignty

ledger.note: 25 September 1920: the Imamate accepts the Sultan's sovereignty with autonomy. The Treaty of Seeb 'granted autonomy to the imamate in the interior of Oman but recognized the sovereignty of the' Sultanate of Muscat. The counterpart names the suzerain here, as the vassal's own side of the event the sultanate-of-oman dossier draws (its /ledger/19 names this state as the vassal); the Imamate page: the interior was ruled by the Imamate and the coast by the Sultanate, 'a de facto split'.

25 October 1954: the autonomy ends in breach of the treaty. 'The entry and occupation of Fahud on 25 October 1954' by the Muscat Infantry was seen by the Imamate as a breach of the Treaty of Seeb and led to the Jebel Akhdar War; the Jebel Akhdar War page dates the war from 10 October 1954 (its infobox). Ghalib al-Hinai had been elected Imam on 3 May 1954.

region.text: the interior and the Jebel Akhdar, from Fahud to Nizwa

ledger.note: 25 October 1954: the Muscat Infantry occupy Fahud and the Jebel Akhdar War begins. The Jebel Akhdar War page: Sultan Said 'first licensed IPC oil prospectors to search for oil near Fahud' (the infobox start is 10 October 1954) and on 13 December 1954 the Muscat and Oman Field Force marched from Fahud to Adam and occupied it; Britain backed the Sultan, Saudi Arabia and Egypt the Imamate.

region.text: Nizwa, the capital, with Firq, Izki, Tanuf, Bahla and the Jebel Akhdar, which the page says the Imamate's forces 'freed' in 1957 (the radius is the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 15 December 1955: the Sultanate takes Nizwa. 'Thereupon, the capital of the Imamate, Nizwa, was captured by the Sultanate on 15 December 1955', and 'the red flag of the Sultanate flew over the interior for the first time in half a century'; the Treaty of Seeb page also has 'In 1955 Sultan Said bin Taimour occupied the capital, Nizwa'. The Jebel Akhdar War page's own timeline puts the advance on Adam in December 1954, so it may be misdated, but both pages give 1955. The sultanate-of-oman dossier has no matching Nizwa gain.

region.text: Nizwa, Firq, Izki, Tanuf, Bahla and the Jebel Akhdar

ledger.note: 1957: the rising frees the Nizwa district. After Talib al-Hinai 'returned to Oman in 1957 with 300 well-equipped Omani fighters', 'the Imamate's forces freed Nizwa (capital), Firq, Izki, Tanuf, Bahla and Jabal Akhdar from the Sultunate's control'; Ibri stayed occupied. The page gives no month and does not date the later suppression of the rising at Nizwa by the Muscat Regiment, so no second loss is entered.

region.text: the interior and the Jebel Akhdar

ledger.note: 30 January 1959: the Jebel Akhdar War ends in the Sultan's victory. 'On 30 January 1959, the SAS occupied Saiq and Shuraijah, and there was little further resistance' (infobox: 10 October 1954 - 30 January 1959, 'Muscati victory'); the Imamate page: the war 'lasted until 1959', with direct British support.

region.text: the interior, abolished as an autonomous Imamate

ledger.note: January 1959: the Imamate of Oman is abolished. 'With the defeat of the Imam, the Treaty of Seeb was terminated and the autonomous Imamate of Oman was abolished' (infobox territorial changes: 'Dissolution of the Imamate of Oman'); Imam Ghalib went into exile in Saudi Arabia, and the Sultanate rules the interior directly. Mirrors sultanate-of-oman's 1959 gain.

wars.name: Omani Imamate rebellion

zones.text: the interior between Ibri and the Sharqiyah

wars.outcome: The Imamate held the interior against the Sultan; the Treaty of Seeb (25 September 1920) left it autonomous under the Sultan's sovereignty, a 'de facto split between Oman and Muscat'.
wars.note: The Treaty of Seeb page names Shaikh Isa bin Salah al-Harthi for the Omani side, Taimur bin Feisal for the Sultan and Ronald Wingate as mediator; neither page mentions towns taken or British troops in 1913-1920.

wars.name: Jebel Akhdar War

zones.text: the interior and the Jebel Akhdar, from Fahud and Adam to Nizwa and the plateau

wars.outcome: The Sultan, with direct British support (RAF raids from July 1958, the SAS on the plateau on 30 January 1959), defeats the Imamate: Nizwa falls on 15 December 1955, the 1957 rising frees the Nizwa district again and the Treaty of Seeb is terminated and the Imamate abolished in January 1959.
wars.note: Infobox 10 October 1954 - 30 January 1959; the Treaty of Seeb page dates the trigger to the occupation of Fahud on 25 October 1954. The Imamate was backed by Saudi Arabia and Egypt (infobox 'Supported by'); Talib bin Ali al-Hinai, the Imam's brother, restarted the rebellion in 1957.

certainty.note: The Hajar Mountains and the Rub' al Khali are natural limits, not surveyed lines; the Treaty of Seeb gives no boundary, only autonomy for 'the interior of Oman'; no page gives a frontier change in 1920-1959, and the fighting of 1954-1959 shows only towns and the Jebel Akhdar plateau, not a front line.

sources.title: Imamate of Oman
sources.note: 1913 rebellion, extent of the Imamate (Ibri to Alsharqiyah), infobox 'End of the Jebel Akhdar War: 1959', Ghalib Alhinai in 1954, 'de facto split'; infobox without area.

sources.title: Treaty of Seeb
sources.note: Signed 25 September 1920 at Sib; terms (autonomy of the interior under the Sultan's sovereignty); capital Nizwa; Salim murdered July 1924 and al-Khalili elected; Ghalib elected 1954; Fahud occupied 25 October 1954; Nizwa occupied 1955.

sources.title: Jebel Akhdar War
sources.note: Infobox 10 October 1954 - 30 January 1959; Nizwa captured 15 December 1955; the 1957 rising; the SAS at Saiq and Shuraijah on 30 January 1959; Treaty of Seeb terminated and the Imamate abolished; Ghalib elected 3 May 1954.

notes: REPAIRED after review (life extended from 25 September 1920 to January 1959). Three pages opened (Imamate of Oman, Treaty of Seeb, Jebel Akhdar War) against a budget of 1-2; the third was opened because the reviewer's finding made the Imamate's last 39 years part of the life. The Treaty of Seeb (25 September 1920) left the Imamate autonomous under the Sultan's sovereignty, not dissolved: the dossier now records that as a vassal_start (the counterpart names the suzerain, the vassal's side of the event drawn by sultanate-of-oman /ledger/19), the end of autonomy at the occupation of Fahud on 25 October 1954, the Jebel Akhdar War (contest 1954-1959), the loss of Nizwa on 15 December 1955, the 1957 rising that freed the Nizwa district, and the dissolve in January 1959 (30 January: SAS at Saiq and Shuraijah; 'the autonomous Imamate of Oman was abolished'). Cliopatria's Imamate row ends in 1919; the 1919 polygon is kept for 1920-1959 as a contested/claimed extent (no page gives a frontier change), so the Nizwa loss and regain are in the ledger but not cut from the shape. Disagreements: the war starts 10 October 1954 (Jebel Akhdar War infobox) or 25 October 1954 (Fahud, Treaty of Seeb page); the Jebel Akhdar War page's 15 December 1955 for Nizwa conflicts with its own timeline (Adam occupied 13 December 1954), but the Treaty of Seeb page also says 1955; the Imamate page gives 749 in the infobox and 750 in the text for the first Imamate; the Imamate page names no ruler list, the Treaty of Seeb page has Salim murdered in July 1924 and al-Khalili elected without a year, and al-Khalili's death is undated (before Ghalib's election on 3 May 1954). The Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi article returned url_not_found, so rulers rest on the Treaty of Seeb and Jebel Akhdar War pages. Not settled: what the Imamate held in 1956 (the Sultanate's flag 'flew over the interior'), the date the Muscat Regiment suppressed the rising at Nizwa, the date of the government-in-exile at Dammam, and whether Ibri (still occupied in 1957) was held by the Sultan from 1955. Counterpart: Sultanate of Muscat and Oman is merged into slug sultanate-of-oman (me-10-c); its dossier has no Nizwa gain for 1955 or loss for 1957 to mirror the two events here, and its 1959 gain, contest_end, vassal and 1954 events mirror this dossier's. Type 'state' rather than 'rebel'. Cliopatria rows: the 1913 and 1919 shapes are the same polygon; the shape includes a coastal cell at Sur that the page does not support.
